% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Non‑zero cells (except colour 3) keep their colour
output(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != 3.

% 3 → 6 when a 4 is immediately to the right
output(R,C,6) :- input(R,C,3), input(R,C+1,4).

% Keep 3 when there is no 4 to the right
output(R,C,3) :- input(R,C,3), not input(R,C+1,4).

% Does the row contain a 2 ?
has_two(R) :- input(R,C,2).

% Zero cells become 4 if the row contains a 2, otherwise stay 0
output(R,C,4) :- input(R,C,0), has_two(R).
output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), not has_two(R).

% Zero cells: only colours 0 and 4 are allowed
:- output(R,C,X), input(R,C,0), X != 0, X != 4.

% If the row does not contain a 2, colour 4 is forbidden (must be 0)

% Other non‑zero cells (V ≠ 0,3) keep their original colour only
:- output(R,C,X), input(R,C,V), X != V, V != 3.

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output cells
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Non‑zero cells keep their original colour
output(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,Color), Color != 0.

output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), not has_two(R).
